title: Sharps, chemicals and unknown materials
audience: Coordinators, support workers and trained cleaners who may be asked to work in a home affected by hoarding or environmental neglect, as part of an authorised support plan. Not a qualification or authority to clear a property, dispose of a resident's belongings, enter by force, or provide welfare or clinical support.
learningOutcomes: Recognise sharps, unlabelled containers and unknown materials as stop-work items.
Isolate the area and escalate to suitably trained personnel without touching the items.
Record the hazard in a log that states what was not done.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers recognition, isolation and referral. It does not cover handling, sorting, testing, transporting or disposing of sharps, chemicals or unknown materials. Completing it does not qualify a worker to do any of these.

instruction.heading: Recognise the stop-work situation
instruction.body: Needles, syringes, lancets, unlabelled containers, leaking bottles and unidentified powders or liquids are stop-work items. Do not pick them up to see what they are, do not sort the material around them, and do not bag them. A loose needle among clothes beneath unknown bottles is a stop-work situation. Cease handling in the area, isolate it and escalate to suitably trained personnel. Keep people, including children and animals, away from the area as far as the plan allows. A photograph of the hazard is taken only where the plan authorises it.

instruction.heading: Record, refer and do not dispose
instruction.body: Prepare a hazard log entry without touching the suspect items. Record the type of item, its location, its condition and the time, and state what you did not do. Request specialist removal through the coordinator. Waste routing, health referral and any notification are decisions for competent personnel. Do not transfer the material into general waste. A skip contractor who declines a leaking, unidentified container has made a correct decision, and the crew should not treat that refusal as an obstacle to be worked around.

procedure: Stop. Step back from the item and keep others back.
Do not pick up, open, sort or move any sharp, container or unknown material.
Isolate the area by the boundary set in the plan, and keep children and animals away.
Record the item type, location and condition in the hazard log, with the time.
Escalate to suitably trained personnel through the coordinator.
Do not dispose of the material in general waste. Wait for the specialist route.

workedExamples.situation: A loose needle appears among clothes beneath unknown bottles.
workedExamples.reasoning: Cease handling, isolate the area and do not touch or sort the material. Escalate to suitably trained personnel and record the hazard log entry.

workedExamples.situation: A skip contractor declines a leaking, unidentified container.
workedExamples.reasoning: The refusal is correct. Do not place the container in general waste. Record it and seek a compliant specialist pathway.

equipmentAndPpe: Hazard log and isolation-boundary tape or signage.
Training-only inert props. No real sharps, chemicals or unknown containers are handled in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Handling an unknown container or needle to see what it is.
commonErrors.prevention: Cease handling, isolate the area and escalate to trained personnel.

commonErrors.error: Putting unknown or leaking containers into general waste.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the item and seek a compliant specialist pathway.

commonErrors.error: Sorting the clothes around a needle to look for others.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop sorting, isolate, and let the trained personnel decide how the search is done.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Sharps and hazardous materials are restricted to suitably trained and, where required, licensed people. Completing this lesson does not qualify a worker to handle them.
No product, method or dilution for any chemical is given in this lesson. Waste and health referral routes depend on local rules, which were not checked for this lesson.

qualityStandard: The learner identifies sharps and unknown containers in a described scene, and stops handling.
The learner isolates the area by the plan's boundary and keeps others back.
The learner records the hazard without touching the item.
documentationEvidence: Hazard log entry with item type, location, condition, time and what was not done.
Referral record to the trained personnel, with the time of escalation.
summary: Needles, sharps and unknown containers mean stop.
Do not touch, open, sort or bag them.
Never place them in general waste.

knowledgeChecks.question: A loose needle appears among clothes beneath unknown bottles. What is the correct response?
options: Pick up the needle with gloves and bag it.
Sort the clothes to find any other needles.
Cease handling in the area, isolate it and escalate to suitably trained personnel.

knowledgeChecks.question: A leaking, unlabelled container is found in a bag of rubbish. What should happen?
options: Stop, record it without opening it, and seek a specialist route.
Put it in general waste to keep the work moving.
Pour the liquid into a drain to empty the container.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should the hazard log record for an unknown container?
options: The contents, after a quick look inside.
The item type, location, condition, time and what was not done.
The price the container might sell for.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a home by force, to clear, sort or dispose of a resident's belongings without valid consent, to handle or dispose of hazardous waste, to deal with unstable stacks or structural hazards, or to provide welfare, clinical or safeguarding assessments. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Work is done only under an authorised support plan and a written agreement with the resident, within the limits set by the employer and the local law. Tenancy, safeguarding and information-sharing rights are jurisdiction-specific, and fire-risk, structural, pest and hazardous-waste decisions belong to the competent authorities and specialists named in the plan. Where authority or consent is unclear, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: consent is not specific, documented and current; the resident has objected or withdrawn consent; a party seeks entry by force, nonconsensual disposal or removal of personal documents; a fire-load, ignition, egress or obstruction hazard is present; a stack or structure is unstable; pests, unknown liquids or mouldy goods are present; sharps, chemicals or unknown containers are found; waste would go to general disposal without characterisation; private information is requested without authority; or the work would go beyond the approved plan. Stopping is a valid professional outcome. Record the disagreement, protect the resident's choices and refer the authority dispute before any property is moved.
